nodes.label: JWT Configuration (docker-compose env)
nodes.author: Jelle van der Graaf
nodes.rationale: JWT_SECRET, JWT_EXPIRE=24h, JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRE=30d configured via environment variables in user-service container to support login and token management

nodes.label: Clean Architecture Pattern (Flutter)
nodes.rationale: Flutter frontend uses clean architecture with DI: lib/frontend (presentation/BLoC), lib/backend (domain/use cases), lib/database (repositories/data sources), lib/di (dependency injection wiring)

nodes.label: Backend Shared Utilities Pattern
nodes.rationale: backend/shared/ contains cross-service db pool, logger (Winston), error classes, auth middleware; enforced as canonical — services must not create local equivalents

nodes.label: UUID Primary Keys Pattern
nodes.rationale: All tables use UUID primary keys for global uniqueness, enabling distributed systems and future horizontal scaling

nodes.label: Health Check Endpoints (/api/health)
nodes.rationale: Each service exposes /api/health, /api/health/ready, /api/health/live for liveness/readiness probes, enabling Kubernetes-style health monitoring

nodes.label: Socket.IO Real-Time Sync (List Service)
nodes.rationale: List service uses Socket.IO WebSocket events (join-list, leave-list, list-updated) for real-time collaborative list synchronization

nodes.label: FR-001.2.2: Rate Limiting (5 per 15min per IP)
nodes.norm_label: fr-001.2.2: rate limiting (5 per 15min per ip)

nodes.label: Freemium Model (Free vs Premium Tier)
nodes.rationale: Free tier provides list management and basic sharing; Premium (FR-009) restricts price comparison and route optimization, enabling low adoption barrier with paid conversion path

nodes.label: Dutch Grocery Market Target
nodes.rationale: Initial focus on major Dutch cities; target supermarkets: Albert Heijn, Jumbo, Dirk, Plus, Hoogvliet, Lidl — chosen for supermarket density and sale-driven pricing culture

nodes.label: WebSocket + Redis Pub/Sub Sync Architecture
nodes.rationale: Flutter client connects via WebSocket; List Service publishes events to Redis pub/sub; WebSocket handler broadcasts to all clients — chosen for real-time collaborative list editing

nodes.label: Dependency Injection Layer
nodes.rationale: DI wires: Data Sources → Repositories → Use Cases → Services, enforcing inward dependency rule so each layer is independently testable via mocking

nodes.label: Freemium Pricing Strategy (€4.99/month)
nodes.rationale: €4.99/month positioned as cost-neutral — app savings exceed subscription cost; target 25% conversion rate from free to premium; annual option planned for Year 2

nodes.label: Self-Hosted NAS Infrastructure Strategy
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted NAS eliminates infrastructure costs (€0/month); designed cloud-ready for migration at 1000+ concurrent users or 70% NAS capacity

nodes.label: bcrypt Password Hashing (cost factor 12)
nodes.rationale: Passwords hashed with bcrypt minimum cost factor 12 (FR-001.1.8) to resist brute-force attacks; same complexity requirements enforced at registration and password reset

nodes.label: Token Blacklist (Redis TTL)
nodes.rationale: Logout invalidates tokens by adding to Redis blacklist with TTL matching token expiration; checked on every request to prevent use of invalidated tokens
